about: Hand-maintained part of the Status page's Elections section (pages/status.html): which election types and periods get a bar, and which independent list, if any, gives each one's known number of contests. Counts come from the site's own results (render/metadata/elections-test2) and data/database/election-provenance.json, by scripts/build-status.mjs. A contest is one constituency, ward or count area at one election; a seat returned unopposed counts as a contest. Calendars are named functions in scripts/build-status.mjs (CALENDARS).

groups.name: Northern Ireland councils before 1973
groups.about: Councils elected before the 1973 reorganisation: county boroughs, boroughs, urban and rural district councils and county councils. No complete list of their elections exists yet, so each bar counts rounds (one council's election on one date) against the known rounds so far: the rounds filed on the site plus rounds documented as not held.

lurgan-borough-council.reason: Triennial election not held: postponed (to October 1971, then indefinitely) because of the reorganisation of local government; the council sat until 1973.
lurgan-borough-council.source: Elections due in May and June 1970 postponed because of the reorganisation of local government: Belfast Telegraph, 10 October 1969, p. 8 (the Bill "postpones triennial local Government elections due to be held in May and June, 1970"); Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1969, p. 2 ("Council elections off until 1971"); Belfast Telegraph, 26 June 1970, p. 3 ("already postponed from this year until October 1971"), OCR text. The councils sat until the 1973 reorganisation.

portadown-borough-council.reason: Triennial January election of Portadown Urban District Council not held: postponed for a year, and again in 1918 and 1919 (the council elected in January 1914 sat on). The next election was the proportional-representation election of January 1920 under the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1919.
portadown-borough-council.source: Parliament and Local Elections Act 1916, s. 2: "the next statutory elections of Borough Councillors and Urban District Councillors were further postponed for one year" (Local Government Board letter, Newry Reporter, 3 October 1916, p. 8); Local Government Board letters postponing urban elections for a further year (Waterford Evening Star, 19 December 1917, p. 4; Tyrone Constitution, 11 January 1918, p. 4); Local Government Board circular of 20 August 1918 "further postponing the holding of urban elections for a year" (Lurgan Mail, 7 September 1918, p. 2); Armagh Guardian, 13 September 1918, p. 1 (OCR text)

portadown-borough-council.reason: Triennial January election not held: the Local Government Act (NI) 1934 moved urban elections to 15 May and extended the councils elected in January 1932 until the election of 15 May 1936.
portadown-borough-council.source: Local Government Act (Northern Ireland) 1934 (Royal Assent: Belfast Gazette, 16 November 1934, p. 379): ordinary day of election moved from 15 January to 15 May; "There will be no election of borough councillors, urban district councillors, or town commissioners in Northern Ireland until May, 1936" (Belfast Telegraph, 4 October 1934, p. 4, on the Local Government Bill, OCR text)
